title: Moving to Garden Ridge After Retirement: 2026 Guide
excerpt: Moving to Garden Ridge after retirement means planning for larger lots, property taxes, car-dependent routines, and access to New Braunfels and San Antonio.

faqItems.q: 1) Is Garden Ridge a good place to retire near New Braunfels?
faqItems.a: Garden Ridge can be a strong retirement fit if you want a quieter Comal County setting, larger lots, and access to both New Braunfels and San Antonio. It is less ideal if you want a dense, walkable daily routine with restaurants and shops close by. The right answer depends on your budget, maintenance comfort, health care access, and how often you expect to drive.

faqItems.q: 2) Are homes in Garden Ridge low-maintenance for retirees?
faqItems.a: Some Garden Ridge homes may be manageable, but larger lots and mature trees can add maintenance compared with smaller subdivision homes. Buyers should evaluate roof age, HVAC systems, drainage, landscaping, fencing, driveway condition, and accessibility details during the inspection period. The goal is to understand the workload before you buy.

faqItems.q: 3) What costs should I budget for when moving to Garden Ridge?
faqItems.a: Budget beyond the purchase price. Include property taxes, homeowners insurance, HOA dues if applicable, utilities, maintenance, repairs, and reserves for exterior or acreage-style upkeep. Retirees should compare the all-in monthly number against income and liquidity before making an offer.

faqItems.q: 4) How close is Garden Ridge to New Braunfels and San Antonio?
faqItems.a: Garden Ridge sits in Comal County between the New Braunfels area and the northeast side of San Antonio. Drive times vary by exact home location, traffic, and route, so buyers should test the drives they will actually make. A few minutes on the map can matter if you have regular appointments, family visits, or airport trips.

faqItems.q: 5) What should I verify before buying a retirement home in Garden Ridge?
faqItems.a: Verify property taxes, exemptions, insurance, utilities, floodplain status, septic or sewer setup, HOA rules, road access, internet options, and inspection findings. You should also compare the home's layout and upkeep needs with how you want to live long term. A local agent can help turn those checks into a practical offer strategy.

opening_question: Is moving to Garden Ridge after retirement a smart fit in 2026?
quick_answer: Moving to Garden Ridge after retirement can make sense if you want a quieter Comal County setting, larger lots, and easy reach to both New Braunfels and San Antonio. The tradeoff is that Garden Ridge is not a dense, walk-everywhere town: homes often sit on larger parcels, errands usually require a car, and property taxes need to be part of the monthly plan. One useful planning marker is that Garden Ridge covers about 7.11 square miles, so a small change in location can change your daily drive, road noise, lot feel, and access to services. For expert updates, contact Cody Posey Real Estate.

content_sections.h: What kind of retirement move does Garden Ridge fit best?
content_sections.p: Garden Ridge works best for buyers who want a Hill Country-style residential setting without moving far from city services. It sits in Comal County, northeast of San Antonio, with quick access toward New Braunfels, Schertz, Cibolo, and the north side of San Antonio. That makes it especially interesting for retirees who want breathing room, but still need medical appointments, airport access, family visits, restaurants, shopping, and day-to-day services within a practical drive. The key is understanding that Garden Ridge is not the same retirement decision as buying a condo near downtown New Braunfels, choosing a lock-and-leave home in a master-planned community, or moving farther into Canyon Lake. Many homes in and around Garden Ridge have a more residential, low-density feel, with mature trees, bigger lots, and fewer neighborhood-style retail conveniences right outside the front door. That can feel peaceful if you want privacy. It can feel inconvenient if you want to walk to coffee, groceries, and restaurants every week. This is where I tell retirement buyers to start with routine, not house photos. Where will you go twice a week? Where are your doctors? How often will you be driving to New Braunfels, San Antonio, Randolph, the airport, or grandkids' activities? A home can look perfect online and still be wrong if the daily pattern does not fit. If you're still comparing broader Hill Country options, my guide to retirement housing options in the Texas Hill Country is a useful companion to this Garden Ridge-specific plan. For a retiree moving in the next 30 to 180 days, the right Garden Ridge search should answer three questions before you tour too many homes: what level of home maintenance you actually want, how much land feels enjoyable instead of burdensome, and whether the location supports your normal week. That is why a custom New Braunfels and Hill Country relocation plan matters more than a generic list of homes.

content_sections.h: What costs should retirees check before buying in Garden Ridge?
content_sections.p: The first cost to study is the all-in monthly number, not just the purchase price. Ownwell's Garden Ridge property tax overview lists a median home value of $859,195 and a median annual tax bill of $6,636. Those numbers are not a promise for any one property, but they show why retirement buyers should look carefully at taxes, insurance, HOA dues if applicable, utilities, maintenance, and the cash reserve needed for a larger home or lot. Texas property taxes can surprise buyers who are moving from states with lower property tax structures. Garden Ridge is in Comal County, and the exact property tax picture depends on the property, exemptions, assessed value, taxing jurisdictions, and whether any special district costs apply. Homestead and over-65 exemptions can matter, but you need to verify timing and eligibility with the appraisal district or tax professional. I never want a buyer to fall in love with a home, then discover after the contract that the monthly number does not match the retirement budget. The second cost is maintenance. A larger wooded lot can be a major part of the appeal, but it can also mean tree work, fencing, driveway upkeep, drainage attention, septic questions on some properties, irrigation planning, and more exterior maintenance than a smaller subdivision lot. This is the part buyers often underestimate because it does not show up cleanly in the listing price. You want the inspection period to evaluate the house and the lifestyle cost of owning that house. The third cost is opportunity cost. Some retirees want acreage feel and privacy. Others would rather put more of their budget into travel, hobbies, family visits, or a lower-maintenance home. Neither answer is wrong. The smart move is to compare Garden Ridge against nearby options before deciding. If monthly payment is still a variable, use the mortgage calculator to test a few price and down-payment scenarios, then have Cody help you translate those numbers into real local choices.

content_sections.h: How should retirees think about location inside Garden Ridge?
content_sections.p: Garden Ridge is small on the map, but the day-to-day experience can still change from one pocket to another. The city website highlights Garden Ridge as "Naturally Home," and that phrase fits the feel many buyers are after: trees, residential streets, and a quieter pace. But quiet does not automatically mean simple. You still want to understand road access, commute patterns, utility setup, internet availability, drainage, and how close the home is to the services you use most. The local detail I see buyers miss is that Garden Ridge is often judged too quickly from a map. Somebody relocating from Austin or California may see the distance to San Antonio, New Braunfels, and Schertz and assume every home will function the same. It does not. A few minutes on the wrong side of a preferred route can change how often you actually go into New Braunfels, whether a quick appointment feels easy, or whether family visits feel routine. I walk clients through that before we write an offer because the house is only part of the retirement decision. You also want to compare Garden Ridge with nearby Hill Country and I-35 corridor choices. New Braunfels gives you more river-town energy and a broader mix of subdivisions, historic areas, and new construction. Schertz and Cibolo may fit buyers who want closer access to Randolph or the northeast San Antonio corridor. Canyon Lake and Bulverde can offer a different Hill Country rhythm. My recent guide on moving to Garden Ridge from California covers more of the relocation comparison, but retirement buyers should go one layer deeper: convenience, upkeep, tax exposure, and future mobility. If you are selling elsewhere and buying in Garden Ridge, timing also matters. You may need a leaseback, a home-sale contingency, or a cleaner transition plan so you are not rushed into the wrong property. That is where a local move plan can reduce stress. Cody can help compare neighborhoods, estimate realistic timelines, and connect the search to the kind of week you actually want after the move.

content_sections.h: What should you verify before making an offer in Garden Ridge?
content_sections.p:
Before you make an offer, verify the basics that affect livability and resale. Confirm the property location, school district as a factual boundary item if it matters for resale, utility providers, floodplain status, septic or sewer setup, well or municipal water status, HOA restrictions, and any city or subdivision rules that affect how you plan to use the property. Garden Ridge also approved a 2026 ordinance allowing golf carts, NEVs, OHVs, and UTVs on designated roadways, according to the city website, so buyers who care about that convenience should verify the current rules, eligible roads, registration requirements, and practical usefulness for a specific home.

Inspection strategy is especially important for retirement buyers because the goal is not just avoiding a bad house. The goal is avoiding a home that creates work you did not want. Roof age, HVAC age, drainage, trees, retaining walls, slope, driveway condition, windows, outdoor structures, and accessibility details all deserve attention. A home may be technically sound but still be a poor fit if it requires more upkeep, stairs, yard work, or future modification than you want.

Financing and cash structure should be sorted before the search gets serious. Some retirees buy with cash from a sale. Others use a mortgage to preserve liquidity. Some need to coordinate the sale of a prior home before they can close. That structure affects offer terms, inspection timing, and how much pressure you feel once the right house appears.

Finally, do not rely on a listing description to tell you if a Garden Ridge home fits retirement life. Build a checklist around your routine, budget, health care access, maintenance appetite, guest needs, and long-term flexibility. Then tour with that checklist in hand. That is the difference between buying a pretty house and buying the right next chapter.

title: Mystic Shores Bulverde HOA Fees: What to Know in 2026
excerpt: Mystic Shores Bulverde HOA fees in 2026 aren't published online. Here's what's public, what you'll have to request from the POA, and what to ask before you buy.

faqItems.q: 1) Why aren't Mystic Shores 2026 HOA fees listed on the POA website?
faqItems.a: The Mystic Shores POA website confirms that the community is a non-profit Property Owners Association and that every owner is automatically a member, but it does not publish a current line-item fee schedule. Detailed 2026 numbers, including the regular assessment, transfer fee at closing, and any pending special assessment, are kept inside the resale certificate and POA financial documents that you request through the management company or pull during your option period.

faqItems.q: 2) What's the difference between an HOA and a POA, and does it matter at Mystic Shores?
faqItems.a: In Texas, both HOAs and POAs are governed by similar property code chapters, and for most buyer questions the practical difference is small. Mystic Shores uses the POA structure because it covers a large, mixed-use planned community with shared amenities and common areas. The bigger point is that membership is automatic with ownership, dues are mandatory, and the POA can enforce restrictions and collect assessments the same way an HOA would.

faqItems.q: 3) Does the Mystic Shores POA fee include boat ramp or lake access?
faqItems.a: It depends on the section, the year, and how the POA has structured its amenity access. Some lake access elements are bundled with base dues, others are billed separately or limited by sticker or wait list during busy seasons. Ask in writing what your 2026 dues include before you assume "lake access" means unrestricted ramp use. A real estate agent who works the area can confirm with the management company directly.

faqItems.q: 4) What is a special assessment and could one hit me after I buy in Mystic Shores?
faqItems.a: A special assessment is a one-time charge approved by the POA on top of regular dues, usually to fund a large repair or improvement that reserves can't cover. It can absolutely happen in any community, including Mystic Shores. The way to evaluate the risk before you buy is to read the reserve study and the recent meeting minutes. Thin reserves plus aging infrastructure equals higher special-assessment risk, and that should be priced into your offer.

faqItems.q: 5) How does buying in Mystic Shores compare to other Canyon Lake or Bulverde communities?
faqItems.a: Mystic Shores tends to attract buyers who want larger Hill Country lots, gated access, and Canyon Lake proximity. Other nearby communities offer different trade-offs on lot size, water access, school district, drive time, and HOA structure. The comparison should be specific to your budget, commute, and how you actually plan to use the property. A local agent can shortlist three or four communities that match your real criteria rather than a generic list.

opening_question: What are the HOA fees in Mystic Shores Bulverde, and why can't you find them online in 2026?
quick_answer: Mystic Shores at Canyon Lake does not publish a public, line-item breakdown of its 2026 POA dues, special assessments, or boat ramp fees. The community is run by the Mystic Shores Property Owners Association, a non-profit POA where every owner is automatically a member, and detailed current numbers have to be requested directly from the management company or pulled from your resale certificate during the option period. Before you write an offer, you'll want the resale certificate, the latest budget, and any pending special assessments in writing. For expert updates, contact Cody Posey Real Estate.

content_sections.h: What's actually public about Mystic Shores POA dues right now?
content_sections.p:
The Mystic Shores POA website confirms the structural basics, but it does not list dollar figures for the 2026 assessment year. What you can verify online: Mystic Shores spans roughly 7,000 acres with about 2,200 home sites and fifty miles of internal road, the Property Owners Association is organized as a non-profit, and every property owner is automatically a member who shares a portion of the cost of common areas, amenities, and gated access. That is it. Everything else, the actual annual assessment, the boat ramp and waterfront access fees, the transfer fee at closing, the reserve study status, and any pending special assessment, is held inside POA documents that are not posted publicly.

The practical takeaway is simple. If a listing description in Mystic Shores quotes a flat "HOA fee" number, that number is a starting point, not the full picture. The full picture lives in the resale certificate, the current operating budget, the most recent annual meeting minutes, and the management company's fee schedule. Those documents are the only place the 2026 numbers are actually binding.

This is also why you'll see wide ranges quoted in random forum threads or older blog posts. The community has grown, the budget has shifted, and some line items are owner-specific (waterfront vs. interior lot, for example). Anything you read online about 2024 or 2025 dues is not a reliable answer for 2026.

content_sections.h: How do you actually get the real 2026 numbers before you buy?
content_sections.p: Three documents do most of the work, and you should be looking at all three before you firm up an offer. First, the resale certificate. In Texas, a seller's resale certificate is the standardized document that lists the current regular assessment, any unpaid amounts on the property, the transfer or capitalization fee due at closing, and any special assessment that has been adopted or is pending a vote. Your option period is the time to request and read this. If anything on it surprises you, that is leverage during the option negotiation, not a fight to have after closing. Second, the current POA budget and reserve study. The budget tells you how this year's dues are being spent, and the reserve study tells you whether the community is funding long-term repairs (roads, gates, amenity replacements) at a healthy rate or is heading toward a future special assessment. A community with thin reserves and aging infrastructure is a community that will likely vote in a dues hike or a one-time assessment within a few years. That is not a deal-breaker, but it should be priced into your offer. Third, the annual meeting minutes and ballot results, usually for the last two years. Minutes tell you what owners are actually fighting about. Short-term rental rules, boat ramp access, gate hours, common-area projects. That context matters more than the dues figure on its own. I've had clients walk away from a beautiful Mystic Shores lot once they read three years of minutes and realized the issue they cared about was still unresolved. For cross-shopping, our river-versus-lake property guide covers how Canyon Lake adjacency, including Mystic Shores, compares to riverfront options nearby on the Guadalupe and Comal.

content_sections.h: Market Reality: what locals know that out-of-town buyers don't
content_sections.p: Mystic Shores does not behave like a typical suburban HOA. Here is what I see again and again with relocating buyers who haven't lived around a large Hill Country POA before. First, the boat ramp and waterfront access piece is not automatic. The community sits near Canyon Lake, but lake access is governed by separate rules and, in some cases, separate fees on top of the base POA dues. Buyers who assume "on the lake" because the development markets that way are sometimes surprised when they realize the lake access they pictured requires additional paperwork, a sticker, or a wait list during peak season. Ask explicitly: what does my 2026 dues number include, and what is billed separately? Second, the lot you buy changes the experience more than the price tag suggests. Mystic Shores is large enough that interior lots, ridge lots with views, and lots that back to the conservation areas feel like different neighborhoods. Drive times to the main gate, line-of-sight to neighbors, well versus public water depending on the section, and septic considerations all vary. I walk clients through this section by section, because the listing photos rarely tell you which version of Mystic Shores you're actually buying. Third, septic, water, and propane are part of the real monthly cost. Most of the community is on private well and septic, not city utilities. Your monthly housing math should include septic pumping every three to five years, a water softener if your well is hard, and propane for heat and cooking on properties without natural gas. None of that is the POA's job, but it affects whether a Mystic Shores home is genuinely cheaper to own than something inside the New Braunfels city limits with municipal services. That comparison is one of the most useful conversations to have before you write an offer, and it ties directly into our guide to buying acreage in the Hill Country, because Mystic Shores lots are sized closer to acreage than to a city subdivision. This is exactly the kind of question I walk my clients through before we ever pull the resale certificate. The dues number is the easy part. The full cost-of-living-here picture is the part you want to have nailed down before you commit.

content_sections.h: How should the 2026 HOA picture shape your offer?
content_sections.p:
Once you have the resale certificate and the budget, the offer becomes a different conversation. A few patterns I use with Mystic Shores buyers in 2026.

If the reserve study is thin and a special assessment looks likely, you can position the offer to account for that risk, either through price or through a closing-cost credit. Sellers and listing agents who have done their homework are not surprised by that conversation. The ones who are surprised are usually the ones who priced based on what the home would have sold for two years ago, not what it is worth now given the documents in hand.

If the transfer or capitalization fee at closing is meaningful, that is a real number that hits your cash to close. Decide upfront whether you want to negotiate that as a seller-paid item, fold it into your closing-cost credit ask, or simply plan for it. Buyers who skip this step find out at the closing table, and that is the worst place to discover an unbudgeted line item.

If the minutes show pending rule changes that affect how you actually plan to use the property, short-term rental rules, boat ramp access, or guest policies, factor that into your decision before you remove your option. Once option ends, those rules come with the property and your leverage to renegotiate is gone.

None of this is meant to scare you away from Mystic Shores. It's a beautiful, well-organized community, and plenty of buyers are very happy there. The point is to walk in with the actual numbers, not the marketing summary, so you can decide on real information.

title: Comal County Home Prices and DOM: June 2026 Market Update
excerpt: Comal County's median sale price sits around $464K–$470K mid-2026 with 96+ days on market and over half of listings failing to sell. Here's what that means.

faqItems.q: 1) What is the Comal County median sale price in mid-2026?
faqItems.a: Comal County's median sale price is sitting between roughly $464,000 (Redfin, closed sales through March 2026, up about 10.5% year over year) and $470,525 (Neuhaus Realty's rolling 12-month MLS average through April). The exact figure varies by data source and time window, but the mid-$460s to low-$470s is the honest 2026 range.

faqItems.q: 2) How many days on market is normal for Comal County right now?
faqItems.a: On the rolling 12-month MLS view, the average days on market is around 96 days. Redfin's recent closed-sales window is showing closer to 118 days. The number that matters more is the spread: well-priced, well-prepared homes are still closing in 30 to 45 days, while overpriced or under-prepared listings are sitting 150+ days or expiring.

faqItems.q: 3) Why are more than half of Comal County listings failing to sell?
faqItems.a: About 50.8% of listings on the 12-month window failed to close. The drivers are pricing strategy that hasn't caught up to current buyer behavior, condition issues in homes that compete against new construction, and missed concession strategy. Buyers in 2026 have time and choice, so anything ambitiously priced or visibly under-prepared gets passed.

faqItems.q: 4) Is now a good time to sell in Comal County?
faqItems.a: It depends entirely on your submarket, your property's condition, and your timeline. A well-prepared home priced tight to ZIP-level comps with a concession strategy in place can still close in 30 to 45 days. A home priced on 2024 numbers without preparation is more likely to land in the 50.8% failed bucket. The right answer requires a market read on your specific situation, not a county-wide yes or no.

faqItems.q: 5) Do new-construction incentives affect resale prices in Comal County?
faqItems.a: Yes, more than most sellers realize. Builders in Bulverde, north New Braunfels, and the Garden Ridge corridor have been carrying significant rate buydowns and closing-cost packages. When a buyer can get a 5.99% rate on a new build with closing costs paid, your resale at the same sticker price is competing on different financial terms. Your list price needs to account for that competition.

opening_question: What is the Comal County median sale price and average days on market heading into summer 2026?
quick_answer: Comal County's median sale price is sitting between roughly $464,000 (Redfin, closed sales through March 2026, up about 10.5% year over year) and $470,525 (Neuhaus Realty's rolling 12-month MLS average through April). Average days on market is now around 96 days on the 12-month view, with Redfin showing closer to 118 days on recent closes. The headline buyers and sellers in New Braunfels and the rest of Comal County need to understand is that more than half of listings (50.8%) failed to sell on the 12-month window. That changes how you price, how you negotiate, and what timing looks like for the rest of 2026. For expert updates, contact Cody Posey Real Estate.

content_sections.h: What do the Comal County numbers actually say in mid-2026?
content_sections.p: Two reliable feeds are telling the same story from different angles. Redfin's closed-sales data through March 2026 puts the Comal County median sale price near $464,000, which is roughly 10.5% higher than the same point a year ago, with average time to sell around 118 days. Neuhaus Realty's rolling 12-month MLS feed, updated through April, has the median at $470,525 and average days on market at 96 days. The two sources differ because one is a monthly snapshot and the other is a 12-month rolling average, but together they paint the picture that matters: the Comal County median is sitting in the mid-$460s to low-$470s, and homes are taking three to four months to sell on average. The stat that should reframe how every Comal County seller thinks about 2026 is this one: 50.8% of listings failed to sell on the rolling 12-month view. That is more than half. It's not that the market collapsed. It's that pricing, condition, and marketing strategy now matter more than they did during the post-pandemic frenzy, when nearly anything listed sold. If you read only one number out of this update, read that one. For a sense of how the market got here, our earlier spring 2026 Comal County breakdown covers the trajectory that led into these numbers.

content_sections.h: Why is the failed-to-sell rate so high in Comal County right now?
content_sections.p: When 50.8% of listings don't close, it almost never means "no one wants to buy." In Comal County in 2026, it means a few specific things, and they are fixable. First, pricing strategy hasn't caught up with the market shift. A lot of homes are still listed at 2024 peak-cycle prices, which were set during a period of compressed days on market and aggressive buyer competition. With 96 to 118 days now the average, the buyer pool has the time and choice to reject anything that looks ambitiously priced. Listings priced ahead of the comps stale out, expire, and show up in that 50.8% bucket. Second, condition matters more than it did two years ago. Buyers who are taking 90+ days to choose a home are not making emotional, scarcity-driven decisions. They are walking through 8 to 15 properties, comparing finishes, and picking the ones that don't require a punch list. Homes that show as "projects" are getting passed unless the price reflects that. Third, concessions are doing more work than headline price cuts. Sellers who close in 2026 are increasingly using closing-cost credits, rate buydowns, and repair credits as a more surgical alternative to a price drop. Buyers facing today's rate environment respond more to monthly-payment relief than to a $10K price chop, dollar for dollar. That's a strategy conversation most listing agents skip and most sellers find out about too late. For reference, the Texas Real Estate Research Center at Texas A&M tracks the broader state housing trend through its monthly Texas Housing Insight, which is a reliable cross-check on the local data above.

content_sections.h: Market Reality: what locals see that the median number hides
content_sections.p: The county-wide median is a useful headline, but it hides three things that matter once you are actually buying or selling here. First, the Comal County median is dragged in different directions by different submarkets. New Braunfels ZIPs 78130 and 78132 trend higher than the county median, especially anywhere along the Guadalupe corridor and the newer-build subdivisions north of town. Canyon Lake (78133) and Spring Branch (78070) trend lower on average price but show wider variance, because waterfront and ridge-lot premiums sit next to interior lots in the same ZIP. If you're pricing a specific home, the county median is the wrong comp. The submarket median, narrowed by ZIP, lot type, and price band, is the only comp that matters. Second, the 96-day average DOM hides a bimodal market. Well-priced, well-prepared homes in desirable submarkets are still selling in 30 to 45 days. Overpriced or under-prepared homes are sitting 150+ days and then either canceling or going stale. There is very little in the middle. What the data calls "the average" is two distributions, not one. Telling clients "expect 96 days" is misleading. Telling them "if you price and prepare right, expect 30 to 45 days, and if you don't, expect 150+ or no sale" is honest. Third, builder incentives are quietly reshaping the resale comps. New construction in Bulverde, north New Braunfels, and the Garden Ridge corridor has been carrying significant rate buydowns and closing-cost packages. When a buyer can get a 5.99% rate on a brand-new build with $10K toward closing, your 2018 resale at the same sticker price is competing on totally different terms. The resale list price has to account for that, or the listing falls into the 50.8% failed bucket. That dynamic ties directly to how sellers should be timing their listing in 2026. This is exactly the kind of read I do for clients before we set a list price. The headline median is a starting point. The submarket math is the strategy.

content_sections.h: How should these numbers shape your buying or selling plan?
content_sections.p: If you are selling in Comal County in the next 30 to 90 days, the play is straightforward but disciplined. Price tight to your specific submarket comps. Prepare the home so it competes with new construction on condition, not just price. Plan a concession strategy upfront, not as a panic move at day 45. And accept that the 96-day average is a guideline, not your target. The goal is to be the property that sells in 30 to 45, not the one that drifts toward 150 and ends up in the failed-to-sell column. If you are buying in Comal County right now, the leverage has shifted in your favor, but quietly. Sellers who have been on the market 60+ days are increasingly open to concessions, rate buydowns, and repair credits that would have been unthinkable in 2024. Your offer should explicitly ask for what you actually need, whether that's a 2-1 buydown, closing-cost credit, or a repair allowance, instead of just shooting at the list price. The data is on your side. Use it. If you are watching the market and not yet ready to move, the next few months matter. Inventory is rising, rates are still elevated, and the 50.8% failed-to-sell rate suggests pricing reset will continue. That's not a forecast and not a guarantee. It's the directional read I'd give a client today. Every situation is different. The only way to know for sure is to run the numbers on your specific property or target neighborhood with someone who knows this market.

content_sections.h: Why does sold-out builder inventory change your buying plan?
content_sections.p: A sold-out builder section usually means the original builder-controlled pricing phase is over. You are no longer dealing with a sales office releasing lots, adjusting incentives, and managing monthly closeout goals. You are dealing with individual homeowners, each with their own reason for selling, their own mortgage situation, and their own tolerance for negotiation. That can create opportunity, but it is not the same opportunity as buying from a builder. With builder inventory, the numbers often revolve around incentives. In nearby active communities, you may see closing-cost credits, rate buydown options, appliance packages, or price adjustments tied to standing inventory. I wrote about that broader pressure in builder incentives in the New Braunfels area, and the same comparison mindset applies along the I-35 and FM 1103 corridor. A resale in Bindseil Farms has to compete with whatever nearby builders are offering at the same monthly payment, not just with other resales. This is also where negotiation changes. A builder may prefer to protect the public price and offer value through credits or financing structure. An individual seller may negotiate on price, repairs, closing date, appliances, or concessions depending on their next move. Neither path is automatically better. They just require different questions before you write the offer. With Bindseil Farms specifically, the old new-construction profile still matters. Livabl shows prior home ranges of about 2,610 to 3,145 square feet, with plans listed from 3 to 5 bedrooms. If payment is the real constraint, run the numbers through the mortgage calculator before you decide which communities belong on your list. Then compare the home itself. A resale may already have window coverings, landscaping, appliances, gutters, water softener equipment, or owner-added improvements that are not included in a base new-build price. A new build may offer warranty coverage, newer systems, and a cleaner handoff, but it can also come with completion uncertainty or upgrade decisions that push the real cost above the advertised number. Those details are not flashy, but they are where buyers often find or lose real money. I would also compare Bindseil Farms against communities with similar buyer appeal, not just anything in the same ZIP code. title: New Braunfels Buyer or Seller Market? 2026 Outlook
excerpt: New Braunfels is buyer-leaning in 2026: Comal County has 7.3 months of inventory, 106 days on market, and homes closing at 92.5% of original list price.

faqItems.q: 1) Is New Braunfels a buyer's market in 2026?
faqItems.a: New Braunfels is buyer-leaning overall in 2026. April Comal County single-family data showed 7.3 months of inventory, 106 days on market, and a 92.5% close-to-original-list-price ratio, all of which indicate that buyers generally have more choice and negotiating room.

faqItems.q: 2) How much below asking price are New Braunfels homes selling?
faqItems.a: The answer depends on whether you compare the final list price or the original list price. Comal County single-family homes closed at 92.5% of original list price in April 2026, while Redfin reported average New Braunfels homes selling around 2% below list price. Price changes made before contract explain part of that difference.

faqItems.q: 3) Is 2026 a bad time to sell a house in New Braunfels?
faqItems.a: Not necessarily. Sellers face more competition and longer marketing times, but correctly priced, well-prepared homes can still attract serious buyers. The April Comal County median price was $429,990, although a countywide median is not a valuation for an individual property.

faqItems.q: 4) Do buyers have more negotiating power with New Braunfels builders?
faqItems.a: Builders may offer rate incentives, closing-cost assistance, or price adjustments on selected inventory, but the terms vary by community and home. Buyers should compare the full monthly payment and ownership cost with nearby resale options rather than judging the offer by the headline incentive.

faqItems.q: 5) What could make New Braunfels shift back toward sellers?
faqItems.a: The market could tighten if buyer demand rises, mortgage rates improve, new listings slow, or available inventory is absorbed. Watch months of inventory, pending sales, days on market, concessions, and price reductions in the specific neighborhood and price band you are considering.

opening_question: Is New Braunfels a buyer's or seller's market in 2026?
quick_answer: The New Braunfels housing market is buyer-leaning in 2026, although the advantage changes by neighborhood, price, condition, and construction type. April data for Comal County single-family homes showed 7.3 months of inventory, while homes took 106 days on market and closed at 92.5% of original list price. Buyers generally have more choices and negotiating room, while sellers need sharper pricing and preparation from day one. For expert updates, contact Cody Posey Real Estate.

content_sections.h: Why does the New Braunfels market favor buyers in 2026?
content_sections.p: A buyer's market does not mean every buyer gets a bargain or every seller is in trouble. It means available supply has moved ahead of the current pace of demand, giving buyers more time, more alternatives, and more room to compare terms. The strongest local signal is inventory. Texas REALTORS data for April 2026 showed 7.3 months of single-family inventory in Comal County, up from 6.0 months a year earlier. A market above roughly six months of supply is generally considered buyer-leaning, especially when that inventory is paired with longer marketing times. The same report counted 2,086 active listings, a 14.8% year-over-year increase. Closed sales were nearly flat at 311, down 0.3% from April 2025. That combination matters more than any single headline about price. More homes are competing for roughly the same number of completed buyers, so buyers can be selective and sellers must earn attention. This builds on the local pattern covered in the recent Comal County June 2026 market update, where price alone did not tell the full story. Time and negotiation data point in the same direction. The average Comal County single-family home spent 106 days on market in April, 23 days longer than a year earlier. The full transaction timeline averaged 139 days from listing to closing, and the close-to-original-list-price ratio was 92.5%. That ratio does not mean every home sells 7.5% below its latest asking price, because listings may have price changes before going under contract. It does show that original pricing expectations are being tested. Broader sources support the local conclusion without making every data set identical. Redfin reported that New Braunfels homes sold for a median of about $337,816 over the three months ending April 2026, with average homes selling around 2% below list and a market competitiveness score of 35 out of 100. Realtor.com's April national report also described a buyer-friendly spring, with slower marketing times and softer list prices. Different platforms use different boundaries and methods, so I do not treat them as interchangeable. The useful common signal is that buyers have more choice and sellers face more competition than they did in the tightest recent markets.

content_sections.h: What does a buyer-leaning market mean for New Braunfels buyers?
content_sections.p: For buyers, the biggest advantage is not permission to submit a low offer on every property. It is the ability to compare the whole deal. You can weigh price against seller-paid closing costs, repairs, rate-buydown help, appliances, survey availability, and the length of the option period. A home that has been listed for 90 days may give you more negotiating room than a clean, correctly priced home that appeared three days ago. Market category sets the backdrop, but the individual listing determines the offer. You should also compare resale homes with new construction carefully. New Braunfels and the surrounding Comal County corridor have substantial builder activity, and builders may use financing incentives or closing-cost assistance that a resale seller cannot match directly. A lower resale price may still be the better long-term choice, while a builder's rate incentive may produce the more comfortable monthly payment. The right comparison includes taxes, HOA or special-district costs, expected repairs, insurance, and financing terms, not just the advertised price. The New Braunfels builder incentives guide explains why buyers need to compare net cost instead of sticker price. This is also a market where due diligence still matters. Extra inventory does not make floodplain questions, drainage, foundation movement, septic systems, property-tax estimates, or the Texas option period less important. It gives you a better chance to slow down enough to evaluate them. Review the seller's disclosure, inspect the property, verify the applicable appraisal district and taxing jurisdictions, and understand how your lender calculates the payment. Follow a clear New Braunfels home-buying process before you start writing offers. What I see buyers miss in New Braunfels is the difference between citywide leverage and property-level leverage. They hear 'buyer's market' and expect every seller to accept a major discount. Then they lose the one updated home in their preferred pocket because it was priced near the recent comparable sales and attracted multiple serious buyers. Your leverage is strongest when a listing has accumulated market time, needs work, competes directly with builder inventory, or started too high. It is weaker when condition, location, price, and presentation all line up.

content_sections.h: How should New Braunfels sellers respond to the 2026 market?
content_sections.p: Sellers should respond with precision, not panic. The April Comal County median single-family price was $429,990, up 7.8% year over year, even while inventory and days on market increased. That is a good reminder that a buyer-leaning market is not the same as a collapsing market. Median price can also shift when the mix of homes sold changes, so it should not be used as a direct estimate of one property's value. Your home's likely range depends on its immediate competition, recent closed sales, condition, lot, age, updates, and whether buyers can purchase a comparable new home nearby. Original list price matters because buyers now have enough options to recognize an ambitious number quickly. When a listing starts too high, the first two or three weeks can pass without serious activity. Later reductions may bring the home into the correct range, but the listing has already accumulated market time and buyers begin asking what is wrong. This is exactly why a New Braunfels pricing strategy should start with current competition and probable buyer objections, not the seller's desired net proceeds alone. Preparation also affects negotiating power. Buyers have alternatives, so small unresolved issues can become reasons to move to the next home or request a larger concession. That does not mean renovating everything. It means handling the visible deferred maintenance, making access easy, presenting cleanly, and documenting updates that matter. If the roof, HVAC, foundation, drainage, or major systems could create uncertainty, decide before listing whether to inspect, repair, disclose, or price for the condition. A buyer-leaning market rewards clarity. The local-only part sellers need to understand is that New Braunfels is not one uniform market. A resale home in 78130 may compete with builder promotions differently from acreage in 78132, an established home near downtown, or a higher-price property in a gated Hill Country community. I walk sellers through the active alternatives a buyer will see on the same search screen, because that is the real competition. A countywide median cannot tell you whether your buyer is comparing your house with three nearby resales, a quick-move-in home, or a different part of the corridor.

content_sections.h: Could New Braunfels market conditions change later in 2026?
content_sections.p: Yes. Market balance can change as mortgage rates, new listings, builder inventory, buyer confidence, employment, and seasonal demand change. A few months of stronger pending sales could absorb inventory. A new wave of listings could push supply higher. That is why the most useful market read is dated and specific. The April numbers describe conditions entering summer 2026, not a guarantee for every month that follows. Buyers should watch three things: how quickly well-priced homes go pending, whether sellers are accepting concessions, and whether their target price band is gaining or losing inventory. Sellers should watch direct competing listings, pending activity, price reductions, and the difference between original list price and final close. These signals are more actionable than a broad forecast. Your decision should also account for your own timing, financing, replacement-home needs, and cost of waiting. Do not confuse a buyer-leaning market with a reason to delay automatically. A buyer who waits for a lower price could face a different mortgage rate, less suitable inventory, or stronger competition later. A seller who waits could benefit from tighter supply, but could also face more competing listings or ongoing carrying costs. Run both scenarios with real numbers. Buyers should estimate payment changes, while sellers can start with a property-specific value review rather than a citywide average. The practical answer for June 2026 is clear: New Braunfels and Comal County are buyer-leaning overall, but the market still rewards good homes and realistic strategy. Buyers have negotiating power, not unlimited power. Sellers can still get strong outcomes, but they have less room for aspirational pricing and weak presentation. Your neighborhood, price point, and competition determine which side has the advantage in your specific transaction.

title: Disabled Veteran Tax Exemption Texas: 2026 Steps
excerpt: The disabled veteran tax exemption in Texas can remove $5,000 to all homestead value from taxation. Here are the 2026 forms, deadlines, and filing steps.

faqItems.q: 1) Do 100% disabled veterans pay property taxes in Texas?
faqItems.a: A qualifying veteran may receive a total property tax exemption on the veteran's residence homestead under Texas Tax Code Section 11.131. The veteran generally must receive 100% disability compensation because of a service-connected disability and have a 100% disability rating, or be considered individually unemployable and paid at the 100% rate. Approval is not automatic; file the required homestead application and supporting documents with the appraisal district.

faqItems.q: 2) What form does a disabled veteran use for a Texas property tax exemption?
faqItems.a: Use Texas Comptroller Form 50-135 for the partial disabled veteran or survivor exemption under Section 11.22. Use Form 50-114, Residence Homestead Exemption Application, for the qualifying 100% disabled veteran residence homestead exemption under Section 11.131. Submit the form to the appraisal district where the property is located.

faqItems.q: 3) What is the disabled veteran exemption amount for a 70% rating in Texas?
faqItems.a: A service-connected disability rating from 70% to 100% can qualify for an exemption of up to $12,000 from one property's appraised value under Section 11.22. That is an exempt value, not a $12,000 tax refund. A separate total residence homestead exemption may apply to veterans who meet the 100% or individual-unemployability requirements of Section 11.131.

faqItems.q: 4) Can a Texas disabled veteran exemption application be filed after April 30?
faqItems.a: Yes, certain disabled veteran exemptions have statutory late-filing provisions. The Texas Comptroller says Section 11.22 applicants may have up to five years after the delinquency date for the property taxes, while other exemption types can have different periods. Contact the appraisal district promptly to confirm the rule that applies to your claim.

faqItems.q: 5) Does a Texas disabled veteran exemption automatically lower a mortgage payment?
faqItems.a: No. The appraisal district must approve the exemption, and a mortgage servicer must update the escrow analysis before an escrowed payment changes. Insurance, HOA dues, principal and interest, and other assessments can remain. Send the approval notice to the servicer and request a written escrow review.

opening_question: How do you apply for the disabled veteran property tax exemption in Texas in 2026?
quick_answer: File the correct application with the appraisal district for the county where the property is located, not with the county tax office. Texas veterans with service-connected disability ratings from 10% to 100% may qualify for a partial exemption, while qualifying veterans rated 100% disabled or paid at the 100% rate because of individual unemployability may receive a total residence homestead exemption. The usual filing deadline is April 30, although Texas law allows late applications for certain disabled veteran exemptions. For expert updates, contact Cody Posey Real Estate.

content_sections.h: Which Texas disabled veteran property tax exemption applies to you?
content_sections.p: The first step is identifying the exemption that matches your disability rating, property, and occupancy. Texas Tax Code Section 11.22 provides a partial exemption for a veteran who is a Texas resident and has a service-connected disability classification from the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs or the applicable branch of the armed services. This exemption can be applied to any one property the veteran owns. It isn't limited to a residence homestead, but it also doesn't erase the full taxable value. The partial exemption amount follows the disability rating. A rating of 10% to 29% can remove up to $5,000 from the property's appraised value. A rating of 30% to 49% can remove up to $7,500, a rating of 50% to 69% can remove up to $10,000, and a rating of 70% to 100% can remove up to $12,000. Veterans who are at least 65 with a rating of at least 10%, totally blind in one or both eyes, or who have lost the use of one or more limbs may also qualify for a $12,000 exemption. These amounts reduce taxable value. They aren't cash payments and shouldn't be treated as a dollar-for-dollar reduction in the tax bill. A different rule applies under Tax Code Section 11.131. A qualifying veteran who receives 100% disability compensation because of a service-connected disability and has a 100% disability rating, or is considered individually unemployable and paid at the 100% rate, may receive a total exemption on the veteran's residence homestead. The distinction matters: the Section 11.22 benefit is a partial value exemption on one property, while Section 11.131 can fully exempt the qualifying homestead from property taxation. Surviving spouses may have continuation rights when statutory conditions are met, so they should use the state guidance and speak directly with the appraisal district rather than assuming the exemption transfers automatically. If you're also evaluating other military housing programs, compare this tax benefit with Texas VLB home loan benefits for 2026. They solve different parts of the ownership cost. The exemption affects property taxes after approval, while the loan program affects financing. I walk veteran buyers through those separate buckets because combining them into one vague idea of a military benefit can produce a bad monthly-payment estimate.

content_sections.h: Which form should you file with the appraisal district?
content_sections.p: For the partial disabled veteran or survivor exemption under Section 11.22, the Texas Comptroller directs applicants to use Form 50-135, Application for Disabled Veteran's or Survivor's Exemptions. Submit it to the appraisal district that appraises the property. The application generally needs documentation showing the service-connected disability rating, so a driver's license or state identification card by itself isn't proof of the VA rating. For a total 100% disabled veteran residence homestead exemption under Section 11.131, use Form 50-114, Residence Homestead Exemption Application. That same form covers the standard residence homestead application and includes the disabled veteran sections. Expect the appraisal district to require identity, ownership, occupancy, and VA disability documentation that supports the exemption claimed. Read the current form instructions before filing because incomplete documentation can delay the decision. New Braunfels is the part that catches relocating buyers. The city crosses the Comal and Guadalupe county line, so a New Braunfels mailing address doesn't automatically tell you which appraisal district handles the home. Properties in much of central and western New Braunfels are handled by Comal Appraisal District, while many eastern New Braunfels properties, including areas toward FM 1101 and Solms, are in Guadalupe County. Check the property's county and appraisal record, then file with that county's appraisal district. Don't send the application to the county tax assessor-collector just because that office later issues the tax bill. This is one of those local details I see military households miss during a PCS. They know they're buying in New Braunfels, but the contract, appraisal district, tax entities, and school district boundaries can change within a short drive. I don't treat a quoted tax rate from a nearby listing as the answer. I verify the actual property record and taxing jurisdictions, then build the payment discussion around that address.

content_sections.h: What is the 2026 deadline, and can you file late?
content_sections.p: The Texas Comptroller lists April 30 as the normal exemption application deadline. If you owned and occupied the residence homestead on January 1, filing by April 30 gives the appraisal district time to process the claim in the regular property tax calendar. Keep a complete copy of the application, supporting documents, and proof of delivery. If the district offers an online portal, save the confirmation page or submission receipt. Missing April 30 doesn't always end the claim. The Comptroller's disabled veteran FAQ explains that applicants for the Section 11.22 disabled veteran exemption, including qualifying surviving spouses and children, may apply up to five years after the delinquency date for the taxes on the property. Certain donated-homestead claims also have extended filing provisions, while some surviving-spouse applications have different late-filing periods. Those rules are specific, and late approval may involve corrections or refunds under the Tax Code. Ask the appraisal district to confirm the correct provision for your facts instead of relying on a generic deadline post. A veteran buying after January 1 should still contact the appraisal district promptly. Eligibility timing, ownership, occupancy, and whether an exemption can apply during the current year depend on the exemption and transaction facts. Your title company, lender, or agent may help you identify the right office and estimate taxes, but the appraisal district decides the exemption. For broader timing context, the Comal County homestead exemption deadline guide explains why filing paperwork and lender escrow adjustments are separate steps. Approval also doesn't guarantee that your mortgage payment changes immediately. If taxes are escrowed, send the approval notice to the loan servicer and request an escrow review. The servicer may need time to update projected tax disbursements, and an existing shortage or other escrowed charges can affect the new payment. Don't spend against an expected reduction until the appraisal district has approved the exemption and the servicer has issued a revised escrow analysis.

content_sections.h: How should the exemption affect your New Braunfels home budget?
content_sections.p: Treat the exemption as an address-specific tax input, not permission to stretch the purchase price. Before making an offer, confirm the property's county, current appraised value, taxing entities, exemption status, and any special district assessments. A 100% disabled veteran homestead exemption can remove the qualifying residence homestead's property tax burden, but it doesn't remove homeowners insurance, HOA dues, PID assessments, MUD charges that aren't property taxes, maintenance, utilities, or loan principal and interest. For veterans receiving a partial exemption, the benefit is smaller than many online examples make it sound. If $12,000 is removed from taxable value, the actual annual savings depends on the combined tax rates that apply to that specific property. The calculation is roughly the exempt value multiplied by the applicable combined rate, subject to the district's final values and rules. That is why the exemption amount and the tax savings aren't interchangeable numbers. I also recommend running two payment scenarios before you commit: one using the tax estimate without the disabled veteran exemption and one using the expected approved exemption. The first protects your budget if processing takes longer than expected or your escrow account hasn't adjusted. The second shows the likely ongoing cost after approval. Veterans using VA financing should also keep the property tax exemption separate from the 2026 VA funding fee rules, because funding-fee exemptions follow their own eligibility and documentation requirements. Your lender should qualify the loan using its underwriting rules and the documentation available at that time. The appraisal district controls the property tax exemption, and the loan servicer controls escrow administration. Cody Posey Real Estate can help you identify the correct local records, compare properties on a consistent monthly-cost basis, and coordinate the questions you need to take to those offices. That gives you a purchase plan built on verified numbers instead of an assumption that every veteran benefit appears automatically at closing.

title: FHA vs Conventional Loan Texas: New Braunfels Guide
excerpt: FHA vs conventional loans in Texas come down to credit, cash, mortgage insurance, and the home itself. Compare the payment and approval tradeoffs before choosing.

faqItems.q: 1) Is FHA always cheaper than a conventional loan?
faqItems.a: No. FHA can require less cash up front for some qualified buyers, but its upfront and annual mortgage insurance can make it more expensive over time. Compare loan estimates using the same price, date, taxes, insurance, and seller-credit assumptions.

faqItems.q: 2) Can a first-time buyer get a conventional loan with less than 20% down?
faqItems.a: Yes. Some conventional programs allow qualified buyers to purchase with far less than 20% down, though private mortgage insurance may apply. Eligibility, pricing, income limits, occupancy rules, and reserve requirements vary by program and lender.

faqItems.q: 3) Does FHA mortgage insurance ever go away?
faqItems.a: It depends on the original loan-to-value ratio and loan terms. For many FHA loans with less than 10% down, annual mortgage insurance lasts for the life of the loan unless the borrower refinances or pays it off; with at least 10% down, it may end after 11 years. Confirm the rule for your specific loan with your lender.

faqItems.q: 4) Will a seller reject an FHA offer in New Braunfels?
faqItems.a: Some sellers may prefer another offer because of appraisal, repair, timeline, or financing concerns, but FHA offers can and do close successfully. A complete preapproval, realistic property choice, clean contract terms, and clear communication can make the offer more credible.

faqItems.q: 5) Which loan is better for a home that needs repairs?
faqItems.a: A standard conventional loan may offer more flexibility when a home has condition issues, while an FHA appraisal applies minimum property requirements. Major defects can still affect either loan, and renovation loan products have separate rules, costs, and approval requirements.

opening_question: Is an FHA or conventional loan better for buying a home in New Braunfels, Texas?
quick_answer: An FHA loan can be the stronger fit when a buyer needs a lower down payment, has a more challenging credit profile, or needs more flexibility in qualification. A conventional loan often works better for buyers with stronger credit who want more property flexibility and a clearer path to removing private mortgage insurance. FHA financing may allow a down payment as low as 3.5% for qualified borrowers, but the best choice depends on the total monthly payment, cash to close, property condition, and how long you expect to own the home. For expert updates, contact Cody Posey Real Estate.

content_sections.h: What is the real difference between FHA and conventional financing?
content_sections.p: The practical difference is not just the minimum down payment. It is how each loan treats your credit profile, mortgage insurance, property condition, appraisal, and long-term cost. FHA loans are insured by the federal government and generally offer more flexible qualification standards. Conventional loans are not government-insured and typically reward stronger credit with better pricing and more mortgage-insurance options. For many New Braunfels buyers, FHA gets attention because qualified borrowers may purchase with 3.5% down. That can preserve cash for inspections, moving expenses, repairs, and the other costs that arrive between contract and closing. Conventional financing can also offer low-down-payment options, so it is a mistake to assume conventional always requires 20% down. Your lender should compare the programs available to you rather than quote one generic minimum. Mortgage insurance is where the long-term math can separate the two choices. FHA loans include an upfront mortgage insurance premium and an annual premium that is generally paid monthly. Depending on the original loan-to-value ratio, FHA annual mortgage insurance may remain for 11 years or for the life of the loan unless the borrower later refinances. Conventional private mortgage insurance can generally be canceled after the borrower meets applicable equity and payment-history requirements. That difference matters if you expect to keep the home and loan for several years. Do not stop at the interest rate. Ask for side-by-side loan estimates that show principal and interest, mortgage insurance, estimated taxes, homeowners insurance, lender fees, and total cash to close. Our New Braunfels mortgage calculator can help you test payment scenarios before you narrow the loan choice with a licensed lender.

content_sections.h: When does FHA make more sense for a Texas buyer?
content_sections.p: FHA often deserves a serious look when the buyer has limited cash, a lower credit score, or debt ratios that make conventional approval or pricing difficult. The program may allow a qualified borrower with a credit score of at least 580 to use the 3.5% minimum down payment. FHA guidelines can permit scores as low as 500 with at least 10% down, although individual lenders may set higher minimums and approval is never automatic. The right question is not whether FHA is a beginner loan. It is whether FHA creates the best combination of approval strength, manageable cash to close, and sustainable monthly payment for your situation. A buyer who keeps several thousand dollars in reserves instead of forcing a larger down payment may be in a healthier position after closing. That cash can matter when the first summer electric bill arrives, an appliance fails, or a move costs more than expected. FHA can also help when a seller is willing to contribute toward eligible closing costs, subject to program limits and the contract terms. Seller credits are not free money and they do not automatically reduce the purchase price. They are a negotiation tool that can lower the buyer's immediate cash burden when the appraisal and loan guidelines support the structure. Review the full Texas closing-cost breakdown before deciding how much cash should go toward the down payment versus prepaid expenses and closing fees. Here is the local part buyers often miss: an FHA preapproval can look comfortable until property taxes are entered for the exact address. New Braunfels crosses Comal and Guadalupe counties, and homes can also carry different city, school district, MUD, PID, or other taxing-unit costs. I walk my clients through the address-level payment before we treat the lender's maximum approval as a shopping budget. The difference between what you can technically qualify for and what you will be comfortable paying every month is where the real decision lives.

content_sections.h: When is a conventional loan the better long-term choice?
content_sections.p: Conventional financing often becomes more attractive when the buyer has stronger credit, stable income, and enough cash to compare several down-payment levels. Better credit can improve the interest rate and private mortgage-insurance pricing. That may produce a lower monthly payment than FHA even when the conventional down payment is not dramatically larger. Property flexibility is another reason buyers choose conventional. FHA appraisals include minimum property requirements tied to health, safety, and soundness. Conventional appraisals also evaluate condition and marketability, but a conventional loan may be easier to use on a home with deferred maintenance that does not fit FHA requirements. This becomes relevant with older New Braunfels housing stock, rural Hill Country properties, and resale homes where peeling paint, damaged flooring, missing fixtures, or other condition issues may need attention before an FHA closing. Conventional financing can also provide a cleaner mortgage-insurance exit. Private mortgage insurance is not necessarily permanent. Federal rules and loan terms can allow borrower-requested cancellation around 80% of the home's original value and automatic termination around 78%, provided the applicable requirements are met. Appreciation alone does not guarantee cancellation, and loan servicers may require a valuation, good payment history, or seasoning period. Still, buyers planning to remain in the home should compare that path against FHA mortgage insurance. The strongest loan is the one that supports the offer and the life you need after closing. If you use every available dollar to make conventional financing work, you may have a better-looking loan but a weaker household balance sheet. If conventional gives you a competitive payment while preserving reserves, it may be the better long-term structure. The student-loan mortgage qualification guide shows why the full debt picture matters more than one headline number.

content_sections.h: How should New Braunfels buyers compare the two loan options?
content_sections.p: Start with the same home price and ask the lender to prepare both scenarios on the same day. Rates and pricing can change, so comparing an FHA quote from one week with a conventional quote from another can distort the result. Use the same estimated property taxes, insurance, HOA dues, closing date, seller credit, and rate-lock assumptions. Then compare the annual percentage rate, monthly payment, cash to close, and five-year cost. Next, test the loan against the types of homes you are likely to pursue. If your search includes older homes near central New Braunfels, properties outside city limits, or homes that need visible repairs, ask how condition could affect each program. If you are focused on newer construction, compare builder-affiliated lender incentives against an outside lender's offer without assuming the larger advertised credit is automatically the best deal. Price, rate, lender fees, and upgrade costs have to be evaluated together. Your offer strategy matters too. Financing type is only one part of the contract. Option-period length, earnest money, appraisal terms, closing timeline, requested seller contributions, and proof of funds all affect how a seller reads the offer. Review Texas option-period and earnest-money basics before you decide that changing loan programs is the only way to make an offer stronger. Finally, build the plan around a comfortable payment, not the top of the approval letter. Texas property taxes and homeowners insurance can change the monthly total materially, and some Hill Country properties add HOA dues, private-road costs, septic maintenance, or well considerations. Your buyer game plan should connect financing, property fit, contract strategy, and cash reserves before you start writing offers.

title: VA IRRRL Refinance Texas: 2026 New Braunfels Guide
excerpt: A VA IRRRL refinance in Texas can lower an existing VA loan payment or improve its terms, but the closing costs and break-even timeline still matter.

faqItems.q: 1) Can I use a VA IRRRL if my current mortgage is not a VA loan?
faqItems.a: No. A VA IRRRL is designed to refinance an existing VA-backed home loan into a new VA-backed loan. Homeowners with a conventional, FHA, or other non-VA mortgage would need to discuss different refinance options with a lender.

faqItems.q: 2) Can VA IRRRL closing costs be rolled into the new loan?
faqItems.a: The Department of Veterans Affairs says eligible closing costs may be included in the new IRRRL loan, which can reduce cash needed up front. Financing costs increases the new balance, so compare the added principal and interest with the expected monthly savings.

faqItems.q: 3) Does a VA IRRRL always require an appraisal?
faqItems.a: An IRRRL often involves a more streamlined process than a standard refinance, and an appraisal may not be required under the VA program. Lender requirements can vary, so confirm the appraisal, valuation, and documentation requirements before relying on an estimate.

faqItems.q: 4) How do I know whether an IRRRL is worth the cost?
faqItems.a: Calculate the total refinance costs, divide them by the expected monthly savings, and compare that break-even date with how long you expect to keep the home. Also compare the new balance, APR, remaining term, total interest, and whether the new payment changed because of escrow assumptions.

faqItems.q: 5) Should I refinance before a PCS move?
faqItems.a: It depends on whether you expect to sell, keep, or rent the home and whether you will own it long enough to recover the refinance costs. Put the IRRRL break-even date beside your earliest realistic PCS or sale date, then coordinate the mortgage decision with your lender and the local real estate plan.

opening_question: Is a VA IRRRL refinance worth it in Texas in 2026?
quick_answer: A VA Interest Rate Reduction Refinance Loan, usually called an IRRRL or VA streamline refinance, can replace an existing VA mortgage with a new VA mortgage at a lower rate or with more stable terms. It may require less documentation than a standard refinance, and the VA says eligible closing costs may be included in the new loan instead of paid entirely up front. The right decision depends on the payment change, total financed costs, break-even timeline, and how long you expect to keep the home. For expert updates, contact Cody Posey Real Estate.

content_sections.h: What does a VA IRRRL refinance actually change?
content_sections.p:
An IRRRL is designed for homeowners who already have a VA-backed mortgage. It replaces that loan with another VA-backed loan, usually to reduce the interest rate, reduce the monthly principal-and-interest payment, or move from an adjustable-rate mortgage to a fixed-rate loan. It isn't a purchase loan, and it isn't the same as a VA cash-out refinance.

The word "streamline" can make the process sound automatic. It isn't. You still apply through a private lender, compare terms, review disclosures, and close on a new mortgage. The streamlined part generally refers to a narrower purpose and potentially lighter documentation than a full refinance. Your lender still has to confirm that the transaction meets VA requirements and its own underwriting standards.

The most useful way to frame the decision is to ask what improves after closing. A lower advertised rate is only one part of the answer. Compare the old payment with the new payment, identify every closing cost being paid or financed, and confirm whether the new term extends your payoff date. If the payment falls but the balance and repayment timeline grow, you need to see that tradeoff clearly before signing.

I walk veteran clients through this as a housing decision, not just a rate decision. A refinance that fits someone keeping a New Braunfels home for another decade may not fit someone expecting PCS orders, a sale, or a move closer to Randolph, Fort Sam Houston, or another JBSA assignment within a year. Your expected hold time changes the math.

content_sections.h: How should Texas veterans calculate the IRRRL break-even point?
content_sections.p: Start with the total cost of obtaining the new loan. That may include lender charges, title-related costs, prepaid items, and a VA funding fee when applicable. The Department of Veterans Affairs notes that closing costs can be included in the new IRRRL loan, which can reduce the cash needed at closing. Rolling costs into the balance does not make them disappear. It means you finance them and may pay interest on them. A basic break-even calculation divides the refinance costs by the monthly savings. If the new loan costs $6,000 and lowers the monthly payment by $200, the simple break-even point is about 30 months. That example is only a starting point. Ask the lender to show the financed balance, interest over the expected holding period, escrow changes, any points, and the effect of resetting the loan term. This is where homeowners around New Braunfels can get tripped up. Property taxes and homeowners insurance are separate from the mortgage interest rate, and escrow changes can blur the comparison. A payment estimate may look better or worse because the tax or insurance assumptions changed, not because the refinance itself created that entire difference. Compare principal and interest separately, then compare the full payment. You should also review the funding fee line instead of assuming it matches a purchase loan. For background, my guide to VA funding fee rates in Texas explains why the fee depends on the type of VA transaction and whether an exemption applies. The lender and VA documentation should confirm the amount for your specific refinance.

content_sections.h: What should you compare before accepting an IRRRL offer?
content_sections.p: Compare the annual percentage rate and total loan costs. The note rate gets attention, but the APR and loan estimate help show the cost of obtaining that rate. One lender may quote a lower rate with more points or fees. Another may offer a slightly higher rate with lower upfront costs. The better option depends on your break-even timeline and plans for the property. Compare the remaining term with the new term. If you are several years into a 30-year mortgage and refinance into a new 30-year loan, your required payment may drop partly because the repayment clock restarted. Ask for an option that keeps the term closer to your remaining years, then compare that payment and total interest with the longer alternative. Confirm the purpose and benefit in writing. A legitimate IRRRL should produce a meaningful financial or payment-stability benefit under VA rules. If the pitch relies on vague urgency, skips the cost breakdown, or focuses only on taking a month off from payments, slow down. The VA specifically warns borrowers to be careful with refinance offers. You don't have to use the company that services your current loan, so comparing written loan estimates is reasonable. Check your likely move date. A military household may be making two plans at once: refinancing the current home and preparing for the next assignment. My VA loan and JBSA PCS checklist covers the broader relocation decisions that can affect whether you keep, sell, or replace a home. An IRRRL should support that plan, not distract from it.

content_sections.h: How does an IRRRL fit a New Braunfels or JBSA move?
content_sections.p: New Braunfels sits between major job centers and several JBSA installations, so a household's next move is rarely just a mortgage question. Commute tolerance, reporting location, deployment timing, property management, equity, and the cost of selling all matter. If you might relocate, calculate the refinance break-even date next to the earliest realistic sale date. What I see locally is that people sometimes treat "keeping the house" as the default because the current VA loan has an attractive rate. Then they discover the actual decision includes rent potential, vacancy, repairs, management, insurance, and the mortgage balance after any refinance costs are added. A good rate can be valuable, but it doesn't turn every property into a good rental or make every PCS timeline predictable. If you expect to sell soon, refinancing may not leave enough time to recover the costs. If you expect to keep the property, a lower payment or fixed rate may improve the long-term plan. If the next purchase is also likely to use VA financing, discuss remaining entitlement and occupancy requirements with a knowledgeable VA lender before making assumptions. Real estate strategy and loan eligibility need to be coordinated, but they are not the same professional opinion. For a wider planning framework, review the Texas veteran home buying plan. It can help you organize lender questions, timing, location, and offer strategy while you decide what to do with the current home. Every situation is different. The only way to know whether the IRRRL supports your move is to run the refinance numbers beside the housing plan.
